findings.title: Do not require numeric Kafka offsets to be contiguous
findings.body: Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be consecutive for records delivered to a consumer: compacted topics and control records can leave gaps even when every delivered record has been processed. This loop stops at the first missing integer, so a partition with completed records at offsets 100 and 102 will never commit past 100 unless offset 101 is delivered—which may never happen. The consumer will repeatedly replay later records after restart and can remain stuck indefinitely. Track completion of delivered records rather than requiring every numeric offset.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so slow workers do not provide backpressure
findings.body: Each worker queue is created without a maximum size, and `submit` can keep adding work while workers are slow. Consequently this mode can accumulate an unbounded backlog in memory instead of slowing consumption as the strategy documentation claims, potentially causing excessive memory growth or an out-of-memory failure during a sustained processing slowdown. Bound the queues and define how submission waits or pauses consumption when they fill.
